content.content:
#### Containers

The "Containers" section is headed "Containers", with a muted line beneath saying that Spec tasks, a Chain prompt's spec steps, and questions always run in a container holding only what their mode may use, and that Code tasks always run on the host, as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says.
First, whether Podman can run them: "Podman" and its version, or "Not installed" with the link to its installation instructions for the platform, and on macOS and Windows, whether its machine is running, with the button that sets it up or starts it, as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says.
Then a row for each harness, in the order of the Agent section: its name, and muted beside it whether it is logged in in its container, "Logged in" or "Not logged in", read from its volume each time the settings open, and a "Log in again" button, which runs its login in a container and shows the login view, as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says, whether it is logged in or not. These are the user's, not the project's, so they are the same with or without a project open.

#### Saving

The prompts, the system prompts and the injected ones, belong to the project opened through the [ProjectDirectoryScope](../project-directory/index.md#project-directory-scope), each saved with the project's data, as the [ProjectDataScope](../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says. Every edit is saved straight away. When the window loads the prompts, any prompt with no file yet has its default saved, so every prompt can also be found and edited by hand. The prompts are read again each time the settings open and whenever another project is opened, so an edit made by hand shows up; a prompt that already shows what was read is left alone, so its cursor stays put.

content.text:
Spec tasks can now be allowed to read the code through a new per-project setting, off by default. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 82 files.

**Changes in the spec:**
- **Containers** (`.claude/reference/scope/container-environment/index.md#spec`):
  - With the setting on, a Spec task or a Chain prompt's spec step gets the code location mounted read only.
  - A writable scratch folder covers only the code's guidance files, `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`, so `piton build` still writes its shape guidance there and never into the code.
  - The run can still write only the spec, the reference, `.piton` and its understanding file.
  - A change takes effect from the next run.
- **Prompts** (`.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#templates`): with the setting on, those runs fill in `CODE_LOCATION`, and get their own paragraph saying the code is read only.
- **Settings** (`.claude/reference/scope/settings-window/index.md#containers`): a "Let Spec tasks read the code" checkbox in the Containers section, shown only while a project is open and saved the moment it's clicked.
- **Project data** (`.claude/reference/scope/project-data/index.md#contents`): a new `.suspense/settings.json` holds the setting.

**Anchors the code should follow:**
- `ContainerEnvironmentScope`: `#spec`.
- `ModeSystemPromptsScope`: `#templates`.
- `SettingsWindowScope`: `#containers`.
- `ProjectDataScope`: `#contents`.
